clue.text: Some parts read in a play about people in a play

blocks.note: the sixteen letters of these four words, taken as written

explanation.surface: Actors read some of their parts aloud in a play about the cast of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'play' seems part of the scene, but 'play about' together signals the reshuffle of the sixteen letters before it. DRAMATIS PERSONAE heads the cast list, and this puzzle's other answers are Shakespeare characters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is the standard heading for the list of characters printed at the start of a script.

clue.text: Journey north from Mexican river presumably without restraint

blocks.note: the Rio Grande, or simply Spanish rio, a river
a northward trip from Mexico goes 'to US'
surface padding that flags the joke in the journey

explanation.surface: Someone travels north from a Mexican river and, presumably, lets loose on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presumably' admits the joke: heading north from a Mexican river takes you TO US, the United States, so the trip reads RIO TO US.
explanation.definitionFit: Riotous behaviour is wild and unruly, the opposite of controlled or restrained conduct.

clue.text: Attractive Amazonian women chasing short man about

ca, circa, means about

explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazonian women' reads as one phrase, but 'Attractive Amazonian' is the definition and 'women' supplies W, which comes last because it is chasing the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The macaw is a brilliantly coloured parrot native to the Amazon rainforest, so a handsome bird of that region.

clue.text: Develop better detailed limits to designs here

definitions.text: Develop better detailed limits to designs here

indicators.note: de-tailed means having its tail removed, so a final letter is dropped
the limits of a word are its two edges, its first and last letters
to develop something is to work it into a different form, so letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the word without its last letter
its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An engineer's instruction: improve your detailed limits for the designs in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a TEST BED is where better designs are developed, so the wordplay also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A test bed is a facility or platform where new machinery or prototypes are trialled and refined before release.

clue.text: Duck and orange starter served in upturned bowls

indicators.note: turned upside down in a down entry, so the word reads from bottom to top
food served in a dish sits inside it, so one piece goes within another
the starter of a meal comes first, so only an initial letter is kept

the first letter

explanation.surface: A menu: duck à l'orange, with an orange starter served in upside-down bowls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck and orange' looks like the classic dish, but 'Duck' alone is the definition, a verb; 'orange starter' is just its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck is to bend down quickly, and to stoop is likewise to lower the head and body forward.

clue.text: Part of sailing ship in which to store dry booty

indicators.note: a store place holds goods inside it, so one piece is put within another

blocks.note: the boom is the spar along the foot of a sail
TT, teetotal, means not drinking

explanation.surface: Pirates stash their dry loot in part of a sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booty' looks like pirate treasure, but it is slang for the backside. Bottom is also the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Booty is informal, chiefly American slang for the buttocks, which is one ordinary sense of the noun bottom.

clue.text: Superficial problem of Belgian region (Belgium not France)

indicators.note: one country's car code replaces another's, so one letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: Flemish describes Flanders, the Dutch-speaking north of Belgium

F is France's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: A political complaint: a shallow problem in a Belgian region, with Belgium blamed rather than France.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads as a political aside, but it is an instruction: put B where F stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish is a small mark or flaw on the surface of skin or an object, a cosmetic fault.

clue.text: Opposite to a 6, perhaps, on a clock face?

definitions.text: Opposite to a 6, perhaps, on a clock face?

blocks.clueFragment: Opposite to a 6, perhaps, on a clock face?
blocks.note: surface reading: the number facing six on a dial is twelve
setter's reading: 6 points to 6-across, the word for the lowest part, and this is its opposite

explanation.walkthrough: On a clock face 6 sits at the base and 12 at the summit; the 6 also points to 6-across, so the answer is the antonym of that entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper end of a dial is its highest point, the reverse of the lowest point where six sits.

clue.text: To look after Old English poetry’s boring

indicators.note: something boring drills into another thing, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: OE is the abbreviation for Old English
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A student's complaint that Anglo-Saxon poetry is tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' seems to judge the poems, but it means drilling into, so the poetry sits inside the Old English abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise or manage work, which is a way of looking after it.

clue.text: Two qualities linked by special criterion

blocks.note: the first quality: touch, as in a deft touch
S is the abbreviation for special
the second quality: tone

explanation.surface: An assessor judges two attributes joined by one special standard.
explanation.walkthrough: The two qualities flank the S that links them. Touchstone is also the clown in As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchstone was a stone used to test gold, so the word came to mean any standard against which things are judged.

clue.text: Gloomy American writer with little time for his job

definitions.text: Gloomy American writer with little time for his job

blocks.note: Edgar Allan Poe, author of macabre tales
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A melancholy American author who barely had time for his own work.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: Poe plus a little time gives the occupation of Poe himself, who wrote The Raven.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe's profession was writing verse, so his job title is the word for a writer of poems.

clue.text: Horse wouldn’t initially be backed into trap

its first letter
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed into trap' sounds like reversing a horse into a trap, the old two-wheeled carriage, but 'trap' is the definition. Cobweb is a fairy in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider's web is a snare built to catch flying insects, a natural kind of trap.

clue.text: Royal Navy’s first cutting costs and first to suffer

prices are costs
its first letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal Navy' reads as one institution, but 'Royal' alone is the definition, used as a noun as in 'the royals'. Each 'first' takes one initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A princess is a female member of a royal family, so in informal use she is a royal.

clue.text: Funny peculiar: 10cc eating a bit of minestrone

blocks.note: the figure 10 read as the letters I and O, followed by CC
its first letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny peculiar' is the old phrase distinguishing odd from amusing, but here the words split: 'Funny' defines, 'peculiar' mixes the letters. 10 is read as the letters IO; 10cc was a British rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic means amusing or causing laughter, the ha-ha sense of funny rather than the strange one.

clue.text: Shylock’s beginning his role having lost a few pounds?

indicators.note: a beginning is the start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: its first letter
Shylock, in The Merchant of Venice, is a moneylender

explanation.surface: Shylock begins his part, having forfeited some of his money or his pound of flesh.
explanation.walkthrough: Pounds suggests Shylock's money and his pound of flesh; here it is body weight. Slender is a suitor in The Merry Wives of Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has shed weight becomes thin and slim, which is what slender describes.

clue.text: Considering playing an extra shot to avoid wet spongy ground

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep it out, so those letters are left out

a bog is marshy ground

explanation.surface: A golfer considers taking an extra shot to keep clear of a marshy patch.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf scene is literal in the wordplay: bogeying means scoring one over par on a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Eying something is looking at it closely, often with a view to acquiring it, so weighing it up.

clue.text: Strange spirit of small Scottish isle

blocks.note: first meaning: odd, an old British colloquialism
second meaning: the liquor distilled from sugar cane
third meaning: one of the Small Isles of the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A whisky drinker finds an odd drink on a tiny island in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings, not two. Rum is one of the Small Isles off Scotland's west coast, alongside Eigg and Muck.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means odd in British slang, names a sugar-cane liquor, and is a Hebridean island.

clue.text: Cluster of buildings in hospital unit lacking in charm

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital
an amulet is a lucky charm
U is short for unit

explanation.surface: A grumble that a hospital complex is ugly and unappealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking in charm' reads as unattractive, but the charm is a lucky one, which loses its U. Hamlet is, of course, the Prince of Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a small settlement, a handful of houses too small to count as a village.

clue.text: Put boats in this Mexican sea belonging to America?

blocks.note: mar is Spanish for sea
in, as in a member who is in a club
A is the abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A question about whether to moor boats in a Mexican sea that belongs to America.
explanation.walkthrough: MAR is Spanish, as spoken in Mexico. Marina is the heroine of Pericles.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a harbour or dock where yachts and pleasure boats are moored, the place where you keep them.

clue.text: Mean to maintain a good posture, mostly failing

indicators.note: when most of a word fails and drops out, only its final letter is left standing

blocks.note: to aver is to maintain or assert
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good
its last letter, all the others having gone

explanation.surface: Someone intends to keep good posture but mostly fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean to' looks like 'intend to', but 'Mean' is the definition, a noun, and 'to maintain' is the verb AVER.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics the mean is the arithmetic average, the sum of values divided by their count.

clue.text: Put together a service led without Latin

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
a Mass is a church service
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A church service is assembled and conducted without any Latin, as after the reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the vernacular Mass, but 'Latin' only supplies the L removed from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate a quantity, which is to put things together.

clue.text: Genre of music heard in Low Country

explanation.walkthrough: 'Low Country' looks like the Netherlands, but 'Low' is a cow's call and 'Country' the definition. The Prince of Morocco courts Portia in The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is a kingdom in north-west Africa, a sovereign nation and so a country.

clue.text: Warm cream coming thirdly on top of cold cream?

over means on top of

explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'cream' looks culinary, but cold cream is a cosmetic, and 'thirdly' applies to all three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold cream is a lotion used to take off make-up, so it is one example of a make-up remover.

clue.text: Many island nations reflected green craze, but not Malta

explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned army rank, so he is a soldier.

clue.text: Rover spaceship Martians seize from below

explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless person who wanders from place to place, a roving vagrant.

clue.text: The original stream split and re-joined anew

clue.text: When one's due in Greek hotel?
